correctness.rationale: With Q={0,...,n-1}, collapse a and rotation b, the two-effective-merge witnesses a b^k a b^t, 2<=k<=n-1, reach every pair of missing states with the asserted lengths. For singleton hole h, F=1+[h+1]_n; for two holes F=the min of admissible orientation witness costs. Direct case analysis under a (add/shift hole) and b (rotate) proves F(new)<=F(old)+1 on every intermediate image with at most two holes. Rank cannot increase, so a path ending with exactly two holes can never leave this domain; potential is universal lower bound and normal witnesses attain it. Simplifying orientation costs yields four cases and complete histogram; n=3 and pairs touching n-1 are included. No finite enumeration is substituted for this all-n proof.
